info.name: DummyJSON API Test Collection
info.description:
# DummyJSON API Test Collection

## Overview

This collection covers automated API testing against the [DummyJSON](https://dummyjson.com/) REST API — a free fake JSON API for prototyping and testing.

**Base URL:** `https://dummyjson.com/`

## Test Cases

| # | Folder | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1-Successful login | Fetches available users, then authenticates to obtain a JWT access token |
| 2 | 2-Get Product and validate its content | Retrieves the full product list, picks a product, and validates its response schema |
| 3 | 3-For user, create a cart and validate | Creates a cart for the authenticated user with at least 3 products and validates the response |
| 4 | 4-Delete operation | Performs a DELETE request on a product and confirms deletion |
| 5 | 5-Negative scenarios | Validates error handling for an invalid category method and an invalid date format |

## Collection Variables

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `usersExist` | Flag set to `true` when users are found; used to conditionally skip the login step |
| `userName` | Username extracted from the users list for authentication |
| `userPassword` | Password extracted from the users list for authentication |
| `userId` | ID of the user used to create the cart |
| `productId` | ID of a product used in single-product and delete requests |
| `existingIds` | JSON array of 3 product IDs used to build the cart |
| `listProducts` | JSON array of product objects (id + random quantity) sent in the cart creation body |
| `productSchema` _(Environment, not Collection, variable)_ | JSON Schema used to validate the structure of a single product response - must be set on the active Postman Environment |
| `token` | JWT access token returned after a successful login |

## Execution Order

Folders and requests are numbered and **must be run in order** (top to bottom). Each folder depends on variables set by the previous one:

- Folder 1 sets `userName`, `userPassword`, `userId`, and `token`
    
- Folder 2 sets `productId` and `existingIds`
    
- Folder 3 uses `userId`, `existingIds`, and `listProducts`
    
- Folder 4 uses `productId`
    
- Folder 5 is independent and can be run standalone
    

> Run the full collection using the **Collection Runner** to execute all test cases in sequence. 
  

## Configuration

`baseUrl` is a collection variable but ships with an **empty default** - select an environment (see `environments/`) before running, or set `baseUrl` yourself. `productSchema` is **not** a collection variable at all: it must be defined on whichever Postman Environment you run against. Both are provided in `environments/DummyJSON - Dev.postman_environment.json` for a zero-setup run against the public API.

item.name: 1-Successful login

request.description:
## GET /users

Retrieves the full list of users from DummyJSON.

**Purpose:** Find a user with valid credentials to use in the login step.

### What this request does
- Sends `GET https://dummyjson.com/users`
- Finds the first user with a non-empty `username` and `password`
- Stores their credentials and ID in collection variables

### Test Assertions
- Status code is `200 OK`
- The `users` array contains at least one entry

### Variables Set
| Variable | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `usersExist` | `true` if a valid user is found, `false` otherwise |
| `userName` | Username of the selected user |
| `userPassword` | Password of the selected user |
| `userId` | ID of the selected user |

## POST /auth/login

Authenticates a user and retrieves a JWT access token.

**Purpose:** Perform a successful login using credentials obtained from the previous request.

### Request Body
```json
{
  "username": "{{userName}}",
  "password": "{{userPassword}}",
  "expiresInMins": 30
}
```

### Pre-request Logic
- If `usersExist` is `false`, the request is **skipped** to avoid a false failure.

### Test Assertions
- Status code is `200 OK`
- `accessToken` is present and not null in the response

### Variables Set
| Variable | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `token` | JWT access token from the response |

item.description:
## Successful Login

This folder implements **Test Case 1**: perform a successful login against the DummyJSON Auth API.

### Flow
1. **1-users** — Sends a `GET /users` request to retrieve all available users. Picks the first user with a valid `username` and `password`, then stores them in collection variables (`userName`, `userPassword`, `userId`). Sets `usersExist = true` if a valid user is found.
2. **2-tokens** — Sends a `POST /auth/login` request using the credentials from step 1. On success, stores the returned `accessToken` in the `token` collection variable.

### Pre-conditions
- The DummyJSON `/users` endpoint must return at least one user with non-empty credentials.

### Variables Set
| Variable | Set By | Value |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `usersExist` | 1-users | `true` if a valid user exists |
| `userName` | 1-users | Username of the selected user |
| `userPassword` | 1-users | Password of the selected user |
| `userId` | 1-users | ID of the selected user |
| `token` | 2-tokens | JWT access token from login response |

item.name: 2-Get Product and validate its content

request.description:
## GET /products

Retrieves the full list of products from DummyJSON.

**Purpose:** Identify a valid product ID and collect the product IDs used for cart creation.

### Test Assertions
- Status code is `200 OK`
- Response envelope (`total`/`skip`/`limit`) has the expected shape
- The first 2 products selected have a valid `id` and `price`

### Variables Set
| Variable | Value |
|----------|-------|
| `productId` | ID of the first product with a valid `id > 0` |
| `existingIds` | JSON array of the first **2** product IDs (used for cart creation) |

item.name: Get a single Product and validate schema

request.description:
## GET /products/:id

Retrieves a single product by ID and validates its response structure.

**Purpose:** Confirm that the product endpoint returns a well-formed response matching the expected JSON Schema.

### URL
`GET https://dummyjson.com/products/{{productId}}`

### Test Assertions
- Status code is `200 OK`
- Response body matches the JSON Schema in the `productSchema` **Postman Environment** variable

### Pre-conditions
- `productId` must be set (by "Get all Products") - if it isn't, the pre-request script calls `pm.test.skip(...)` and `pm.execution.skipRequest()`, so this shows up as an explicit **skip** in the run results, not a failure.
- `productSchema` must be set on the **active Postman Environment** - it is not a collection variable and is not shipped with a default. See `README.md` → Configuration for the schema to use.

item.description:
## Get Product and Validate Its Content

This folder implements **Test Case 2**: retrieve a product and validate its content and schema.

### Flow

1. **all products** — Sends a `GET /products` request to retrieve all products. Picks the first valid product and stores its `id` in `productId`. Also stores the first 2 product IDs as a JSON array in `existingIds` (used later for cart creation).
    
2. **get a single product and validate schema** — Sends a `GET /products/{{productId}}` request and validates the response body against a predefined JSON Schema stored in the `productSchema` collection variable.
    

### Pre-conditions

- The `productSchema` **Postman Environment** variable must contain a valid JSON Schema string (not a collection variable - see README).
    

### Variables Set

| Variable | Set By | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | all products | ID of the first valid product |
| `existingIds` | all products | JSON array of the first 2 product IDs |

item.name: 3-For user, create a cart and validate
Create cart with at least 3 products

request.description:
## POST /carts/add

Creates a new cart for the authenticated user containing at least 3 products.

**Purpose:** Validate that a cart can be created with multiple products for a specific user.

### Request Body

``` json
{
  "userId": {{userId}},
  "products": {{listProducts}}
}

 ```

`listProducts` is a JSON array of `{ "id": , "quantity": }` objects, built dynamically in the pre-request script.

### Pre-request Logic

- Reads `existingIds` (product IDs set in folder 2)
    
- Skips the request if fewer than 3 ids are available, via `pm.test.skip(...)` + `pm.execution.skipRequest()` - shows up as an explicit **skip** in the run results, not a failure
    
- Maps each ID to an object with a random quantity using `{{$randomInt}}`
    
- Stores the result in `listProducts`
    

### Test Assertions

- Status code is `201 Created`
    
- The `products` array matches `existingIds` 1:1 (id + quantity)
    
- The cart belongs to the authenticated `userId`
    
- `totalProducts`/`totalQuantity`/`total`/`discountedTotal` are internally consistent
    

### Pre-conditions

- `userId` must be set (from folder 1)
    
- `existingIds` must contain at least 3 product IDs (from folder 2)

item.description:
## Create a Cart and Validate

This folder implements **Test Case 3**: create a cart for the authenticated user containing at least 3 products, and validate the response.

### Flow

1. **Create cart** — Sends a `POST /carts/add` request with the `userId` from folder 1 and a list of products (at least 3) built from `existingIds` (set in folder 2). Each product is assigned a random quantity via `{{$randomInt}}`. The pre-request script constructs the `listProducts` variable before the request is sent.
    

### Pre-conditions

- `userId` must be set (from folder 1).
    
- `existingIds` must be set (from folder 2) and contain at least 3 product IDs.
    

### Validations

- Response status is `201 Created`.
    
- The `products` array in the response matches `existingIds` 1:1.
    
- Cart totals (`totalProducts`, `totalQuantity`, `total`, `discountedTotal`) are internally consistent.
    

### Variables Set

| Variable | Set By | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `listProducts` | Pre-request script | JSON array of `{ id, quantity }` objects |

item.name: 4-Delete operation

request.description:
## DELETE /products/:id

Deletes a product by ID.

**Purpose:** Validate that the DELETE operation returns a successful response confirming the product was deleted.

### URL
`DELETE https://dummyjson.com/products/{{productId}}`

### Test Assertions
- Status code is `200 OK`
- Response body contains `isDeleted: true`

### Pre-conditions
- `productId` must be set (from folder 2)

> **Note:** DummyJSON simulates deletion — the product is not actually removed from the database. The API returns a mock deletion response.

item.description:
## Delete Operation

This folder implements **Test Case 4**: perform a DELETE operation on a product and confirm it was deleted.

### Flow
1. **delete a product** — Sends a `DELETE /products/{{productId}}` request using the product ID set in folder 2.

### Pre-conditions
- `productId` must be set (from folder 2).

### Validations
- Response status is `200 OK`.
- The response body contains `isDeleted: true`.

> **Note:** DummyJSON simulates deletion — the product is not actually removed from the database, but the API returns a response as if it were.

request.description:
## GET /products/category/:category (non-existent category)

**Negative Scenario:** Sends a GET request using a randomly generated lorem word as the category slug.

### Purpose
Verify that the API returns a `200 OK` with an empty product list when the category does not exist.

### Pre-request Logic
- Generates a random lorem word and stores it in the `category` variable.

### Expected Behavior
- Status code: `200 OK`
- `products` array is empty

## GET /products/category/10 (numeric category slug)

**Negative Scenario:** Sends a GET request using a number (`10`) as the category slug.

### Purpose
Verify that the API returns a `200 OK` with an empty product list when the category slug is a number (no category named "10" exists).

### Expected Behavior
- Status code: `200 OK`
- Response has the standard paginated structure (`products`, `total`, `skip`, `limit`)
- `products` array is empty

## GET /products/category/ (empty category slug)

**Negative Scenario:** Sends a GET request with an empty category slug in the URL path.

### Purpose
Verify that the API returns a `404` error when no category name is provided.

### Expected Behavior
- Status code: `404`
- Response body contains: `Product with id 'category' not found`

exec: pm.variables.set("category", pm.variables.replaceIn('{{$randomLoremWord}}'));

request.description:
## POST /products/category/:category (wrong HTTP method)

**Negative Scenario:** Sends a POST request to an endpoint that only supports GET.

### Purpose
Verify that the API returns a `404` error when an unsupported HTTP method is used on the category endpoint.

### Pre-request Logic
- Generates a random lorem word and stores it in the `category` variable.

### Expected Behavior
- Status code: `404`
- Response body contains an error matching `Cannot POST /products/category/<category>`

## GET /products?modifiedAfter={{$randomDateFuture}}

**Negative Scenario:** Filters products by a `modifiedAfter` date set in the future.

### Purpose
Verify that the API returns an empty product list when no products have been modified after a future date.

### Query Parameters
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| `modifiedAfter` | `{{$randomDateFuture}}` — a dynamically generated future date |
| `select` | `rating,meta` |

### Expected Behavior
- Status code: `200 OK`
- `products` array is empty
- `total`, `skip`, and `limit` are all `0`

### Why this is a negative test
No products should exist with a modification date in the future. This validates that the filter works correctly and returns an empty result set rather than all products or an error.

exec:
const moment = require('moment');

pm.variables.set("modifiedAt", moment(pm.variables.replaceIn('{{$randomDatePast}}')).format("DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss"));

request.description:
## GET /products?modifiedAfter={{modifiedAt}} (invalid format)

**Negative Scenario:** Filters products using a `modifiedAfter` date in an invalid format.

### Purpose

Verify that the API returns a `400 Bad Request` error when the `modifiedAfter` parameter is not in ISO 8601 format.

### Pre-request Logic

- Uses `moment.js` to generate a past date formatted as `DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss` — an intentionally invalid format
    
- Stores the result in the `modifiedAt` environment variable
    

### Query Parameters

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `modifiedAfter` | `{{modifiedAt}}` — a past date in `DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss` format |
| `select` | `rating,meta` |

### Expected Behavior

- Status code: `400 Bad Request`
    
- Response body contains: `Invalid 'modifiedAfter' - should be a valid ISO 8601 date`
    

### Why this is a negative test

The API requires dates in ISO 8601 format. Passing a non-standard format should be rejected with a clear validation error.

item.description:
## Negative Scenarios

This folder implements **Test Case 5**: validate that the API handles invalid or unexpected inputs gracefully.

Two sub-folders cover different API endpoints:

### Product Categories (sub-folder)
Tests targeting the `/products/category/:category` endpoint:
- **negative scenario search** — Sends a `GET /products/category/pets` request with a body (invalid for GET). Expects a `404` response with an error message indicating the method is not allowed.
- **Category is numeric** — Tests behavior when a numeric value is passed as the category.
- **Category is empty** — Tests behavior when an empty string is passed as the category.
- **Category wrong Method** — Tests using an incorrect HTTP method on the category endpoint.
- **Category does not exist** — Tests a category name that does not exist in the system.

### Filter Products (sub-folder)
Tests targeting the `/products?modifiedAfter=` filter:
- **date in the future** — Passes a future date as `modifiedAfter`. Expects a `200` response with an empty products array (`total: 0`), since no products were modified after a future date.
- **Invalid date format** — Passes a date in an invalid format (`DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss` instead of ISO 8601). Expects a `400` response with the message: `Invalid 'modifiedAfter' - should be a valid ISO 8601 date`.

### Pre-conditions
- These scenarios are independent and do not require variables from earlier folders.
